title: Venture Capital Careers
description: WHO IS RENEW CAPITAL? At Renew Capital, we see opportunities in Africa where others, too often, only notice the problems. We invest, rather than provide handouts, by finding promising businesses, connecting them to a global network of investors and growing them into world-class companies. We do this because we believe that many growing businesses, together, create the engine that lifts entire nations out of poverty. Our ambition is to become the best middle market investment firm in Africa, investing in at least 27 countries — half of continent — by 2027. We’re looking to hire those who embody our values and get excited about our vision for a prosperous Africa with growing businesses, thriving nations and a legacy of investment. Since establishing the Renew Capital presence in Africa in 2012, we have been pioneering an innovative blended-finance model that partners with the development community and focuses on investing in high-potential small and medium enterprises (SMEs). This blended-finance model allows us to invest in smaller deals that are often overlooked by larger investors but are too big for microfinance. We then help these companies build disciplined, gender-smart management systems and teams and grow them into market leading companies. As a result of our investment work to date, Renew Capital has mobilized millions of dollars into businesses in Africa, and our network of investors, the Renew Capital Angels, has become an active investor network with more than 180 members. We are inviting passionate and qualified candidates to apply to join our team. In candidates, we look for professionals with a trailblazing attribute who align with our organizational values of intelligence, integrity, beauty and grit. We welcome challenges and face them head-on each and every day! What we do is not easy, but it is rewarding and forces us to grow and innovate. As such, we hire individuals who are committed to their work, take pride in what they do and are relentless in advancing projects forward in a systematic manner. The people that flourish at Renew Capital are mission-driven; they see the big picture and the long-term result of their work, and they sincerely wish to make a lasting economic impact on the continent of Africa. If this sounds like you, we encourage you to apply.

title: Fashion Designer

With 77 endorsing countries and the EU, CHAMP aims to unlock the potential of multilevel partnerships to accelerate NDC implementation, improve access to climate finance for subnational governments, and showcase pioneering action on climate mitigation and adaptation. Reporting to the Senior Director, Finance and Private Sector, and working closely with the Senior Urban and Regional Economist and the NDC Partnership, this position requires expertise in public and blended finance, strong diplomatic skills to engage with Ministries of Finance, multilateral banks, and development finance institutions, and the ability to turn country-level lessons into systems-level change. What You Will Do Programme Delivery (60%) Lead design, delivery, and monitoring of Climate Finance workstream to ensure coherence between global finance reform efforts, country platform design, and on-the-ground technical assistance in Kenya and Colombia. Produce actionable analysis and insights capturing enabling conditions for subnational climate finance, drawing from country experiences and global practice, and translate findings into practical recommendations for governments and finance actors. title: Consultancy for the adaptation and finalization of the EMAP+ resource package for Ethiopia (POWER program)
description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Under the program's Safety Outcome 4, which holds that the social norms of community members support the rights of diverse women and girls and prevent and condemn VAWG, the program works to reduce VAWG and promote positive behavior change through evidence-based approaches. In Ethiopia, this work sits within the POWER program (2025–2027), supported by Irish Aid. POWER pursues holistic GBV prevention and response across Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan and Sudan, delivered through strengthened women-led organizations. Its design reflects a set of deliberate commitments: at least 25 percent of funding flowing directly to partners, adherence to the PEERS principles for equitable partnership, women-led safety audits, a dedicated emergency response pillar, and a partnership learning pillar. This consultancy contributes directly to Sub-outcome 2 of the Irish Aid project. To ensure that the EMAP+ Resource Package is relevant and effective in the Ethiopian context, the program will engage a consultant to lead the adaptation, review and finalization of the EMAP+ materials. Consistent with POWER's partnership learning pillar, the contextualization is documented so that the reasoning, and not only the finished product, is available to others. The consultant will refine the overall resource package, validate its relevance through remote engagement with the IRC Ethiopia team and partners, and document the adaptation decisions taken so that the process is traceable and reusable. This consultancy contributes directly to the achievement of Sub-outcome 2 of the Irish Aid project. Rwanda’s Country Platform serves as a coordination and investment mechanism to align public, private, and development finance around the country’s climate, restoration, and green growth priorities. By bringing together government, investors, development partners, and implementing organizations, the Platform aims to accelerate the development and financing of high-impact initiatives that support sustainable economic growth, climate resilience, and landscape restoration. Restoring Africa’s Landscapes Requires a Comprehensive Approach That Addresses Every Aspect Of The Restoration Journey. WRI Africa’s Blueprint Outlines Four Essential Areas Of Focus Develop Capacity: To ensure they are ready to receive funding and deliver impact, Restore Local provides targeted training and builds the capacity of restoration champions. Deploy Finance: Through innovative financing mechanisms that blend public, private, and philanthropic capital, Restore Local directly funds champions who restore vitality to the land. Through its TerraFund program alone, it has made $17 million in investments to date. Secure Policy: Restore Local supports government institutions in creating plans and policies that fund and monitor restoration. It connects policymakers with each other and with technical experts through programs such as the Landscape Policy Accelerator. Monitor, Report, Verify, Learn: Through the TerraMatch platform, which combines cutting-edge geospatial data with on-the ground verification, Restore Local enables restoration champions to share the impact of their work with their community, peers and investors. Job Highlight As the Head of Green Finance & Investment, you will play a strategic role in advancing Rwanda’s climate and green growth agenda by translating priority initiatives into investment-ready opportunities and mobilizing capital for high-impact solutions. This position provides an opportunity to shape Rwanda’s emerging climate finance landscape by connecting government priorities, development finance, private capital, and innovative financing approaches to accelerate investments in restoration, climate resilience, and sustainable growth. You will strengthen WRI’s capacity to engage with government institutions, development finance institutions, commercial investors, philanthropic organizations, multilateral funds, and private sector actors to develop financing solutions and investment opportunities that support Rwanda’s climate and sustainable development priorities. You will report to the Climate, Economics, and Finance (CEF) Program Director, WRI Africa with a dotted reporting line to the Senior Director, Restoration Finance. You will work closely with the Rwanda Country Representative, VIA Foundation, Rwanda Green Fund (RGF/FONERWA), and relevant WRI Africa and Global teams. Facilitate collaboration among public, private, and development finance stakeholders to identify, structure, and advance investment opportunities.
